objective: T-20260929-03: does buying US merger targets at the next open after the 8-K announcement and holding a fixed 20/60 sessions survive 10/20 bp costs and re-dated placebos?

sources.core_claim: High initial target price (day-1 close over offer price) ratios are associated with significant negative abnormal returns of 3.5% over the two months following the announcement; consistent with investor overreaction.
sources.project_applicability: Direct evidence on the post-announcement window this iteration trades: a subset of targets (high price-to-offer) subsequently under-perform, so an unconditional 20/60 day hold can be diluted or negative. Motivates reporting drift by 1-20 day CAR rather than assuming positive drift.
sources.reflection: Full PDF text saved as snapshot; abstract quoted verbatim. Limitations: Working paper draft April 2015; conditions on offer price which we do not have in the 8-K pipeline; sample and cost treatment not audited here.

sources.core_claim: The merger arbitrage spread has declined by more than 400 bps since 2002; the decline is economically and statistically significant and part of it is likely permanent (increased arbitrage capital, reduced transaction costs).
sources.project_applicability: Explains why a plain post-announcement long in targets should earn little after our 10-20 bp per side costs: the day-1 spread already compresses most of the deal premium; only the small residual is available at next-open entry.
sources.reflection: Full text saved as snapshot; abstract quoted verbatim. Limitations: Sample ends around 2008-2009; does not cover 2020s; hedge-fund index returns, not stock-level next-open entries.

sources.core_claim: 4,750 mergers 1963-1998: risk-arbitrage excess return about 4% per year after transaction costs and the non-linear (put-like) payoff; returns correlate with the market in downturns.
sources.project_applicability: Classic upper bound for hold-to-close arbitrage: single-digit percent annual excess return with put-like tail, which is far below this workbench's admission bars once 10-20 bp per side is charged on fixed-horizon trades.
sources.reflection: Page summary snapshot; 4% figure corroborated in the same-session search summary. Limitations: 1963-1998 sample, hold to resolution, hedged long-short; only the publisher page summary was read, not the full paper.

sources.core_claim: Across 51,000+ US takeover-type events 1992-2021 small stocks earn disproportionately large gains BEFORE deals are announced because of less analyst coverage.
sources.project_applicability: Warns that in the small-cap tier the bulk of the target premium may already be in the price at the 8-K; hence pre-announcement CAR must be reported and the t3 variant is a real test, not a favored bet.
sources.reflection: Abstract summary snapshot. Limitations: Abstract only, claim_only; full text paywalled.

sources.core_claim: Merger-arbitrage excess returns are negatively related to arbitrage capital (limited arbitrage) and are economically and statistically significant in 1981-1996.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the premise that fixed-horizon target holds can earn a premium only when arbitrage capital is scarce; recent decades have more capital, so the recent window is the fair test.
sources.reflection: claim_only; not used to set any threshold. Limitations: SSRN returned 403; only search-engine summary and the Wikipedia/Jetley-Ji citations were read.

sources.core_claim: Target CARs of 14-32% accrue up to and including the announcement date and start days to weeks before it (Keown-Pinkerton 7 days, Jarrell-Poulsen 15 days, Schwert 42 days).
sources.project_applicability: Defines the leakage check: report the [-5,-1] CAR before the 8-K; if the premium is already earned pre-8-K there is nothing left to trade at next open.
sources.reflection: claim_only. Limitations: Search-result summary of a survey paper; the PDF (Glasgow eprint) was not opened as text.

sources.core_claim: Deal break rates 8% (2,182 mergers 1990-2007) to 22.7% (1901 mergers 1981-1996); friendly deals close 82%, hostile 38%; transaction costs significantly erode arbitrage returns.
sources.project_applicability: Break risk is why we do not condition on completion: DEFM14A/closing data would select survivors, so only fixed-horizon holds are tested.
sources.reflection: Page summary snapshot. Limitations: Secondary summary of academic studies.

sources.core_claim: The SEC efts.sec.gov full-text search endpoint is free, key-less, covers 2001 onward, returns form/items/CIK/accession per hit.
sources.project_applicability: Data source for the free EDGAR merger-agreement 8-K pipeline; confirmed locally that hits are per file with items lists.
sources.reflection: Endpoint probed locally the same day. Limitations: README of a third-party wrapper; fair-access User-Agent and <=10 req/s still apply.

sources.core_claim: Registry row (queued): 2025-10 working paper abstract claims Sharpe >2.1 after costs for 30-day post-announcement target returns (claim_only, full text paywalled); 1992-2021 study says small-cap target gains arrive before announcement.
sources.project_applicability: The row this iteration resolves; the >2.1 Sharpe is a weak prior only and no threshold is copied from it.
sources.reflection: Read from the registry, not independently verified.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: No hold-to-close variant: spreads have compressed and completion status would select surviving deals; only fixed-horizon holds are tested.
Small targets may have gained before the 8-K; the t3 card tests it and the [-5,-1] CAR is reported.
